items.title: JetBlue Unveils New Domestic First Class Seats as It Hopes to End Losing Streak
items.summary: JetBlue’s new domestic first class seats seek to give customers a more premium experience with customized cocktails, meals, and roomy seats made with mattress foam. The carrier is banking on the seats to help it turn a profit.

items.title: What Happens to a Travel Company Owned by Private Equity for Too Long?
items.summary: One of travel's best tour operators went to market and couldn't sell. The reasons tell you as much about where the industry is headed as about the company itself.

items.title: AirDNA Enters Revenue Management Market With Host Dynamic Pricing Tool: Exclusive
items.summary: Short-term rental hosts are leaving money on the table if they don't at least dabble in dynamic pricing. If AirDNA can make the process easier for hosts, then there is a big upside awaiting.

items.title: Airbnb Names Ex-Booking.com Hotel Boss and Tripadvisor Exec as Chief Business Officer
items.summary: If Airbnb needs people connections and know-how to scale its boutique hotels business, it found someone with deep experience in Pepijn Rijvers. He also has marketing and tours and activities experience at Booking.com and Viator, respectively.

items.title: The F&B Strategy That Starts With Winning Over Locals, Not Just Guests
items.summary: As hotel owners look for growth beyond the guest room, restaurants and bars are playing a more central role in how a property attracts locals, builds identity, and generates revenue. Paris Society, part of Ennismore and the wider Accor Group, offers a model for turning F&B ve

items.title: Vrbo Brings Sponsored Listings to Vacation Rental Search
items.summary: For vacation rental managers, Vrbo’s new ad product could unlock more business. The question is whether managers see incremental demand — or pay more just to stay visible.

items.title: Fosun Files for ClubMed IPO in Hong Kong
items.summary: ClubMed's revenue rose less than 2% last year, suggesting that "premiumization" isn't delivering pricing power yet. An IPO would generate capital that might help fix that.

items.title: Marriott Presses Sales Teams on $1.55 Billion ‘Gap to Goal’ for 2027 Groups
items.summary: Marriott has given sales teams a year-end stretch goal of $1.55 billion for group bookings for next year at the hotels it manages in the U.S. and Canada. Its global 2027 group sales look "flattish." Other companies are more upbeat.
